claims.text:
J.R.R. Tolkien noted that it was a custom in the Took family to use high-sounding names and that he turned them into old names of Frankish and Gothic origin.
The name Isumbras is of Anglo-Saxon and French origin and means "iron-arm". It contains the Anglo-Saxon and Middle High German element isen ("iron") and the French element bras ("arm").
Tolkien likely got the name from Sir Isumbras, an English medieval romance about a man who suffers a lifetime of hardship but who finds happiness in his latter years.
